title: Sidecar Proxy and Control-Plane Separation: Reference Architecture for Private Deployments
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview
========
This document describes a recommended reference architecture for separating the control plane from the data plane using a lightweight sidecar proxy pattern in Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). The goal is to provide a deployable, secure, and observable topology that enables independent lifecycle, safe rollouts, and clear operational responsibilities for customers and Redwood engineers.

Audience
--------
- Private-deploy solution architects
- Customer SRE/Platform engineers
- Redwood field engineers and support teams

Scope and goals
----------------
- Scope: production private deployments using Redwood runtime components (runtime-workers, kv-cache, frontdoor) behind customer networking. This covers both VPC-hosted private control plane and fully on-prem installations.
- Goals:
  - Minimize blast radius during control-plane changes.
  - Allow per-tenant control plane upgrades independent of data-plane sidecars.
  - Provide secure, observable sidecar-to-control-plane communication with enforced policy and fallback behavior.
  - Document validated networking, certificate, and firewall requirements for customer acceptance testing.

Key concepts and terminology
----------------------------
- Data plane: GPU inference workers, runtime processes, and local caches that serve token-level inference.
- Control plane: management and control services (rollouts, config store, auth broker) that do not directly serve inference traffic but coordinate runtime configuration.
- Sidecar proxy: lightweight per-node/local process that mediates outbound control-plane communications and provides health checks, local caching of policies, and mTLS termination for runtime components.
- Split responsibilities: data plane focuses on fast token paths; control plane handles policy, feature flags, and lifecycle control.

High-level architecture (textual diagram)
----------------------------------------
Customer Network (VPC or On‑prem)
  |
  +-- Runtime Nodes (gpu-node-01..N)
  |     - runtime-worker (inference process)
  |     - local-kv-cache (optional)
  |     - sidecar-proxy (local, e.g. envoy/consul-proxy shim)  <---> Control Plane (Redwood-managed or customer-hosted)
  |
  +-- Edge Gateway (optional) -- egress NAT / specialized routing for telemetry and metrics

Description: each runtime node runs a sidecar that performs:
- mTLS connection brokering to the control plane
- local policy evaluation and fallback (in case control plane not reachable)
- caching of small control-plane responses (rollout config, token bucket allowance metadata)
- health checks and graceful drain coordination during upgrades

Design decisions and rationale
------------------------------
1) Why separate control plane?
   - Faster data-plane upgrades and scaling without affecting global control-plane state.
   - Administrative boundaries: customers can own network and firewall rules for control-plane egress while Redwood operates the control plane if agreed.
2) Why a sidecar rather than direct runtime-to-control-plane connections?
   - Centralize TLS and auth responsibilities; avoid duplicating cert rotation logic in resource-constrained runtime artifacts.
   - Enable consistent observability and local cache behavior across nodes.
3) Fallback behavior
   - Sidecar must implement a local default policy for short outages (config TTL default 5m). Long outages (>=30m) enter degraded-mode and emit an alert.

Networking and security requirements (acceptance matrix)
--------------------------------------------------------
| Requirement | Direction | Port/Proto | Purpose | Customer test checklist |
|-------------|-----------|------------|---------|------------------------|
| Control-plane egress | Node -> Redwood control-plane | 443/TCP | API, rollouts, metrics | curl https://control.redwood.example/health (succeeds) |
| Telemetry_ingress | Node -> telemetry.proxy | 8080/TCP or 443/TCP | Metrics/Traces | Verify metrics visible in Redwood console within 2m |
| mTLS between sidecar and control-plane | Node <-> Control Plane | 443/TCP | Auth and encryption | Validate cert chain, CN match expected |

Note: customers with strict outbound policies should permit specific IP ranges (provided per-deployment). Avoid opening wide CIDR blocks; prefer egress via proxy chain.

Sidecar responsibilities and behavior
-------------------------------------
- Auth: present node identity using client cert signed by customer KMS-integrated CA or Redwood-issued cert (per contract).
- Policy cache: maintain a small cache with TTL and LRU eviction to survive short control-plane outages.
- Healthcheck proxy: provide a local /healthz that returns combined runtime and control-plane sync status.
- Draining: on SIGTERM, sidecar coordinates a graceful drain with runtime-worker and signals readiness false after inflight tokens complete (configurable threshold).

Operational runbook: deploy, validate, and day‑2 checks
-----------------------------------------------------
1) Pre-flight (before install)
   - Validate node OS and kernel network settings (see compatibility table).
   - Confirm outbound egress rules to allowed control-plane CIDRs and telemetry endpoints.
   - Provision CA/PKI approach: customer-managed CA OR Redwood-managed issued certs.
2) Install steps (ordered)
   a. Install sidecar binary and local config bundle
   b. Install systemd unit / container service with restart=on-failure
   c. Start sidecar and validate /healthz returns OK
   d. Start runtime-worker and ensure it registers with local sidecar
3) Post-install validation (smoke tests)
   - Put a small sample request through runtime-worker and assert latency and correctness
   - Verify control-plane config fetches within 10s of startup
   - Assert metrics flow (node-level and request-level) to telemetry backend
4) Day‑2 checks (daily/weekly)
   - Cert expiry: run cert-check daily and notify owners if <14 days
   - Cache TTL miss rate: monitor cache_misses / minute; target <0.1%
   - Successful control-plane syncs per hour: >99.9%

Upgrade and rollback strategy (control plane and sidecar decoupled)
------------------------------------------------------------------
Principles:
- Never perform a control-plane global change and a sidecar binary upgrade at the same time for the same customer without a staged canary.
- Use staged rollouts: 1% -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% with pause-and-validate steps.

Control-plane-only changes (safe path):
1. Publish change to control plane that carries versioned config schema.
2. Sidecars fetch new config but refuse to apply if runtime-worker version incompatible (sidecar enforces schema compatibility).
3. Monitor canary nodes for 30 minutes; if metrics within thresholds, proceed.

Sidecar binary upgrades (safe path):
1. Canary 2–3 nodes with sidecar restart policy and extended logging; run synthetic inference traffic for 15m.
2. Confirm health, metrics, and metric parity with previous version (latency, error-rate).
3. If rollback needed: systemctl rollback to previous sidecar unit or, in containerized installs, redeploy previous container image tag.

Explicit rollback checklist (short form)
1. Pause traffic routing to canary nodes (if using traffic-shift).
2. Revert sidecar package to previous version and restart.
3. Confirm local /healthz and control-plane sync success.
4. Reintroduce canary traffic and validate (15m).
5. Continue rollout or abort.

Metrics, SLOs and alerting thresholds
------------------------------------
- Control-plane-sync-latency (median): target < 200ms in VPC; < 500ms on-prem (due to potential networking constraints). Alert if p99 > 2s for 5m.
- Sidecar-healthy-percent: target > 99.5%. Alert if <99% for 10m.
- Policy-cache-miss-rate: target <0.5%. Alert if >2% sustained for 10m.
- Degraded-mode-duration: alert when a node is in degraded-mode > 30m.

Compatibility and hardening checklist (table)
-------------------------------------------
| Component | Minimum | Recommended notes |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|
| OS | Ubuntu 22.04 / RHEL 8 | Use vendor LTS with up-to-date kernel for networking stability |
| Container runtime | containerd 1.7+ or Docker 20.10+ | Ensure CRI configs do not drop NET_RAW cap if required |
| Kernel params | net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1 | See appendix for full sysctl list |
| TLS | TLS1.2 minimum, TLS1.3 recommended | mTLS enforced between sidecar and control-plane |
| Ports | 443, 15000 (local admin) | Avoid port conflicts with host services |

Security considerations and PKI options
--------------------------------------
- Customer-managed CA: preferred for regulated customers. Sidecars are provisioned with signed certs via automated CSR flow and must support short-lived cert rotation (default TTL 7 days).
- Redwood-issued certs: available for customers who permit Redwood to manage cert lifecycle; certs are rotated server-side and sidecars validate chain via embedded root.
- HSM/KMS integration: for customers requiring private key protection, integrate CSR signing through KMS-bound signing flows.

Appendix: Example sidecar config snippet (YAML)
-----------------------------------------------
# minimal sidecar config
proxy:
  listen_address: 127.0.0.1:15000
  control_plane_url: https://control.redwood.internal
  tls:
    client_cert_path: /etc/sidecar/certs/client.pem
    client_key_path: /etc/sidecar/certs/client.key
    ca_path: /etc/sidecar/certs/ca.pem
cache:
  policy_ttl_seconds: 300
  max_entries: 1024
health:
  readiness_path: /healthz
  readiness_grace_seconds: 5

Appendix: Smoke test commands
-----------------------------
1) Validate control-plane reachability from node:
   curl -sS --cacert /etc/sidecar/certs/ca.pem https://control.redwood.internal/healthz
2) Validate sidecar local health:
   curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:15000/healthz
3) Sample runtime request (basic):
   curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' | jq

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Node-side ownership: customer platform / SRE (primary for network and host OS)
- Redwood on-call: control-plane incidents and sidecar regressions (secondary for sidecar binary issues under managed packages)
- Escalation path: contact field-engineering Slack channel + open support ticket with "private-deploy-sidecar" tag

Acceptance criteria for customer go‑live
---------------------------------------
- All runtime nodes report sidecar healthy percent >= 99% for 24h
- Control-plane sync p99 < 2s for 24h in test traffic window
- Cert rotation path tested and successful (simulate 7-day expiry)
- Latency and error-rate for sample requests within agreed SLOs in contract

-------------------------------
